name: Ramadan
intro:
The blessed month of Ramadan is a month full of memories. The days 1, 3, 4, 6, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23 and 24 recall critical moments in the history of Islam. Both joyful memories and sorrowful days are found in this month.
The birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS) and the Ascension (Mi'raj) of the Prophet (SAWW) are two joyous events of this month. The deaths of Abu Lahab, Ibn Muljam, Aisha, Marwan, Ziyad ibn Abihi and Hajjaj al-Thaqafi are days of the destruction of the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS). On the other hand, the martyrdom of Lady Fatima al-Zahra (AS) according to one account, the striking and martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), the passing of Lady Khadija (AS) and Lady Nafisa (AS), and the martyrdom of Mukhtar are days of grief for the family of Muhammad (AS).
The battles of Badr, Ta'if and Tabuk and the Conquest of Mecca are history-making days of Islam. The ascension of Jesus (AS) to the heavens, the revelation of the Qur'an, the ceremony of the pact of brotherhood, and the rain prayer by the Prophet (SAWW) are also important historical events.
The innovation of the Tarawih prayer by Umar, the arrival of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr in Egypt, the pledge of allegiance to Imam Mujtaba (AS), the arrival of the letters of the people of Kufa to Imam Husayn (AS), Muslim's departure toward Kufa, the crown princeship of Imam Reza (AS) and the minting of coins in his name — each recalls chapters from the pages of Islam.

events.text: On the first night of the blessed month of Ramadan, performing the ritual bath (ghusl) and visiting Imam Husayn (AS) have been recommended.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: pp. 4-5.

events.title: The Crown Princeship of Imam Reza (AS)
events.text: On 7 Rajab of the year 200 AH, Ma'mun the Abbasid wrote a letter to Imam Reza (AS) and summoned that noble figure to Merv to be his crown prince. On the first day of Ramadan in the year 201 AH, the people pledged allegiance to Imam Reza (AS) as crown prince; some have reported it as the sixth of this month.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rajab volume, p. 63.
Fayz al-'Allam: p. 24. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 49, pp. 303, 321, 11.

events.title: The Death of Marwan
events.text:
On this day in the year 65 AH, Marwan ibn al-Hakam, at the age of 81, rushed to the depths of Hell in Damascus; his caliphate lasted 9 months.
Marwan was the son of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As and was nicknamed “the lizard, son of a lizard.” He and his father were cursed by the Prophet (SAWW); even Aisha said to Marwan: I bear witness that the Prophet (SAWW) cursed your father while you were in his loins.
Marwan strove greatly in enmity toward God, the Prophet (SAWW) and the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), especially Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), from the time of Uthman until the end of his days. After Uthman — contrary to the command of the Prophet (SAWW) — brought him and his father al-Hakam back from Ta'if to Medina, he gave Marwan the one-fifth (khums) of Ifriqiya, granted him Fadak as well, and made him his minister and secretary.
During Uthman's caliphate he stirred up sedition. In the Battle of the Camel he shot an arrow and killed Talha, and after the victory, when he was taken captive, he made Hasan and Husayn (AS) his intercessors and Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) released him. They said to the Imam: Take his pledge of allegiance. He said: Indeed his hand is the hand of a Jew — for the Jews are known for scheming and trickery. After Marwan joined Muawiya, whenever the governorship of a city was given to him, he was zealous and insistent in promoting the cursing of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). In Medina, every Friday he would climb the pulpit of the Prophet (SAWW) and, in the presence of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, curse Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). After the destruction of Yazid, Marwan took his place, married his wife, and ruled for nine months. Yazid's wife, al-Zuhri, put poison in his food so that he lost his speech, and finally she placed a pillow over his mouth and, together with the maidservants, sat upon him until he reached his end on the first of the month of Ramadan.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 83. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 385.
Shifa' al-Sudur: vol. 1, p. 323. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 78, 84.

events.title: The Battle of Tabuk
events.text:
On the first of Ramadan in the year 9 AH, the Battle of Tabuk took place. This battle is also called “al-Fadiha” (the exposer), because the hypocrites of Medina and those who intended to kill the Prophet (SAWW) at the mountain pass were disgraced and exposed. The army that took part in this battle is called “Jaysh al-'Usra” (the Army of Hardship), because they set out amid great difficulty and toil, even though it was the season of gathering the harvest. The army's departure was in the month of Rajab, and 30,000 people set out, of whom only a thousand were mounted. The Prophet (SAWW) said: “Bring plenty of footwear with you,” and along the way every two men satisfied their hunger with one date, and water was also scarce. In this battle some women also accompanied the Prophet. On the other hand, 82 of the hypocrites of Medina made excuses and did not go to war, remaining in Medina so that in his absence they could plunder his house and drive his family out of Medina. The Prophet (SAWW) appointed Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) as his successor in Medina, and the hypocrites said words that hurt the blessed heart of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). The Prophet (SAWW) said to him: Are you not content to be to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me...?
On the return from Tabuk, forty of the hypocrites who were with the Prophet decided that when the Prophet's camel reached the top of the pass, they would fill gourds with pebbles and roll them beneath the camel's feet so that the camel would bolt and the Prophet (SAWW) would fall from it and be killed. At the time of carrying out the plot, the Prophet's camel did not move a step, the scheme of the hypocrites failed, and God protected the sacred person of the Prophet (SAWW).
Meanwhile, the hypocrites who had remained in Medina plotted against the life of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and dug a long pit along the road of Medina and covered it with mats, so that when Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) came out to welcome the Prophet (SAWW), he would fall into that pit on his return and they would fall upon him and kill him. But on his return, the Imam's horse would not cross over the mats and the pit, and once again the trick of the hypocrites came to nothing.
No fighting took place at Tabuk, and the Prophet returned to Medina with the army. The occurrence of this expedition in the month of Rajab has also been reported.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 158.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 61. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, pp. 91-93.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 60.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 91.

events.title: The Passing of Lady Nafisa (AS)
events.text:
On this day in the year 208 AH, the devout and ascetic Lady Nafisa Khatun (AS), daughter of Hasan ibn Zayd ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), passed away in Egypt.
Her husband was Ishaq al-Mu'taman, son of Imam Sadiq (AS), and through her mother she is linked to the Moon of the Banu Hashim (AS) (Abbas).
Lady Nafisa (AS) had dug a grave for herself and constantly prayed and completed recitations of the Qur'an in that grave.
She fell ill on the first of Rajab and wrote a letter to her husband, who was in Medina, informing him of her condition. On the first night of Ramadan her illness worsened, and the next day, while she was fasting, a physician was brought and he ordered her to break her fast. She said: “How astonishing! For thirty years I have asked God to let me depart this world in a state of fasting, and now that I am fasting, should I break it?” Then she began reciting Surah al-An'am, and when she reached the blessed verse “For them is the abode of peace with their Lord,” she passed away.
Her husband arrived after she had passed away. He wanted to take her to Medina and bury her in Baqi' beside her pure forefathers, but the people of Egypt detained him with pleading and requests. Ishaq al-Mu'taman saw the Prophet (SAWW) in a dream, who said: “Do not oppose the people of Egypt in this matter, for because of Nafisa, God sends down His mercy and blessings.” Ishaq buried her body in its present location, and it is well known that supplication beside her grave is answered.
sources: The Life of Sayyida Nafisa (AS): pp. 43-45.
Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 187.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 289. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 195-196.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Lady Fatima al-Zahra (AS)
events.text: According to one account, the martyrdom of the truthful and pure Lady Fatima al-Zahra, the well-pleasing (AS), took place on this day.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 167; vol. 43, pp. 189-214.

events.title: The Death of Ziyad ibn Abihi
events.text:
Ziyad ibn Abihi perished in Kufa in the year 53 AH. He is known as Ziyad ibn Abihi (“son of his father”), Ziyad ibn Ummihi (“son of his mother”), Ziyad ibn Ubayd and Ziyad ibn Sumayya; and because Ziyad's father was unknown due to the multiplicity of possibilities, he was called Ziyad ibn Abihi.
When he joined Muawiya, he was named Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan and became Muawiya's brother, and he acknowledged his mother's adultery. Sumayya was a slave woman of Harith ibn Kalada the physician. Harith had set her to shepherding sheep, but Sumayya's vile and lustful nature brought so much shame in the desert that Harith drove her away. After that, Sumayya attached herself to Ubayd, a shepherd of Thaqif, and was officially counted among the prostitutes of Ta'if, and she also stained the reputation of Ubayd's family.
Brotherhood with Muawiya was one of the means Muawiya employed to win Ziyad to his side. He arranged a gathering and used a number of people as witnesses there, among them Abu Maryam, the wine seller of Ta'if. He stood up and said to Ziyad: One night Abu Sufyan came to Ta'if and asked me for a prostitute. That night there was no one except Sumayya. We waited until the comings and goings lessened. I sent Sumayya to him. Ziyad accepted his mother's adultery and became Muawiya's brother! And to make him believe this kinship, Muawiya sent his sister to his house and ordered her to remove her veil, since he was now her mahram.
After becoming Muawiya's brother, Ziyad began disavowing Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), killing the Shi'a of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and plundering their property. Cutting off hands, ripping open bellies, hanging on the gallows, burying alive, driving red-hot pins into the eyes of the Shi'a, beheading children, demolishing houses and setting them on fire were among his deeds. He buried Abd al-Rahman ibn Hassan alive in a grave for the crime of loving Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS).
In Basra and Kufa he killed thirteen thousand people for being Shi'a or for the possibility of being Shi'a, and then wrote to Muawiya: I have carried out your wish to this extent, and these deeds were done with my left hand. If the governorship of the Hijaz is given to me, I will do the same with my right hand, which is idle, and I intend to demand of the people of Iraq in the mosque that they publicly disavow Ali (AS) and praise the House of Umayya. Whoever does not accept, I will kill him and destroy his house. When this news spread, Imam Hasan (AS) and the Shi'a cursed him, and some saw Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in a dream cursing him, and that accursed one, before carrying out his decision, was struck with plague and arrived in the depths of Hell.
sources: Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 114. al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 74. Fayz al-'Allam: p. 23. Shifa' al-Sudur: vol. 1, p. 310.
Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 16, p. 187. al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: Ramadan volume, p. 75. Shifa' al-Sudur: vol. 1, p. 312. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 87.
Shifa' al-Sudur: vol. 1, p. 315. Citing Ibn Khallikan and Ibn al-Athir.

events.title: Minting of Coins in the Name of Imam Reza (AS)
events.text: On this day in the year 201 AH, a gold coin was minted in the blessed name of Imam Reza (AS). According to one account, this day was the day of the Imam's forced crown princeship, and the people pledged allegiance to him as crown prince.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 278. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 195.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 6. Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 115.

events.title: The Arrival of the Letters of the People of Kufa to Imam Husayn (AS)
events.text: In the year 60 AH, a group of Kufans brought letters from the people of Kufa to Imam Husayn (AS). Among them were the names of Sulayman ibn Surad, Musayyab ibn Najaba, Rifa'a ibn Shaddad al-Bajali, Habib ibn Mazahir and a group of the Imam's Shi'a, and the letters were delivered to the Imam (AS) by Abd Allah ibn Mus'ma' al-Hamdani and Abd Allah ibn Wal.
sources: al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 112. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 333.

events.title: The Passing of Lady Khadija (AS)
events.text:
On this day Lady Khadija al-Kubra (AS) departed from this world. According to one report, this is 45 days after the passing of Abu Talib (AS). Other views on the date of her passing are as follows: 23 Rajab, 27 Rajab, the end of Rajab, the first of Ramadan, and 12 Ramadan. She passed away after Abu Talib (AS) at an interval of three days, according to one account one month, according to another 45 days, and according to another 50 days.
She was the first wife of the Prophet (SAWW), and as long as Khadija (AS) was alive, the noble Prophet of Islam (SAWW) took no other wife. Her precedence in accepting Islam and her services to the Prophet (SAWW) are too many to mention. It suffices as to her virtue that she is the honored mother of Lady Siddiqa Tahira (AS), and all the descendants of the Prophet (SAWW) trace back to her. At the time of her passing she gave several bequests to the Prophet (SAWW), and despite all her sacrifice and expenditure of wealth, she said to the Prophet (SAWW): “O Messenger of God, forgive me for any shortcoming on my part toward you.” The Prophet (SAWW) said: “Never! I saw no fault in you; rather you exerted the utmost effort and endeavor on my behalf. You bore great hardships in my house. You spent your wealth in the way of God.” Then Khadija (AS) said: O Messenger of God, I entrust this daughter to you (and she pointed to Lady Fatima (AS)). After me this girl is an orphan and a stranger. Let none of the women of Quraysh harm her. Let no one strike her face, raise a shout at her, or cause her any distress.
She is the first woman to have believed the Prophet (SAWW), the first woman to pray in congregation with the Messenger of God (SAWW) in Mecca, the first woman to declare her faith in Mecca among the polytheists, the first woman to defend the Messenger of God (SAWW) against the enemy and to give all her wealth to the Prophet (SAWW), and the first woman whose faith reached perfection through accepting the guardianship (wilayah) of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). One day the Prophet (SAWW) called Khadija (AS), seated her beside him and said: This is Gabriel, and he says: Islam has conditions, which are: affirming the oneness of God Almighty, affirming the messengership of the messengers, affirming the Resurrection and the principles and rulings of this Shari'a, obeying those in authority and the pure Imams from his descendants one after another, together with disavowing their enemies.
Khadija (AS) affirmed all of them and acknowledged the pure Imams, especially Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). The Prophet (SAWW) said: “He is your master and the master of the believers and their Imam after me,” meaning “Ali is your master, the master of the believers after me, and their Imam.” Then he took a firm covenant from Khadija (AS) on accepting the guardianship of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). Then the Messenger of God (SAWW) explained one by one the principles and branches of religion, even the etiquette of ablution, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, jihad, maintaining family ties, and the obligatory and forbidden acts.
Then the Prophet (SAWW) placed his hand over Amir al-Mu'minin and Khadija (AS) placed her hand over the hand of the Messenger of God (SAWW), and in this manner she pledged allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
sources: al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 127. Fayz al-'Allam: p. 27. Masar al-Shi'a: pp. 6-7. Nafa'ih al-'Allam: pp. 191, 115.

events.title: The Ceremony of the Pact of Brotherhood
events.text: On this day in the first year of the Hijra, the noble Messenger of Islam (SAWW) established a pact of brotherhood among his companions and made Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) his own brother.
sources: al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 112. Fayz al-'Allam: p. 31. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 7. Taqwim al-Muhsinin: p. 14. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 46.

events.title: The Death of Hajjaj al-Thaqafi
events.text:
In the year 95 AH on such a day, the cruel, bloodthirsty and vile Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi perished. During the reign of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, in the city of Wasit, which he himself had built, he reached his end with a disease of the stomach (akila, a gangrenous or cancerous ailment). Other views on the day of his death are 21, 23, 25 and 27 Ramadan.
His mother was named Qariha, who before marrying Yusuf ibn Aqil, Hajjaj's nominal father, had been in the house of Harith ibn Kalada the physician. When Hajjaj was born he had no anal opening, and the physician made one for him. Also, he would not nurse until a black goat was slaughtered and some of its blood was smeared on his mother's breast and on Hajjaj's face, and from the fourth day he accepted the breast. For this reason Hajjaj became bloodthirsty and used to say: My greatest pleasure is in shedding blood. This is not surprising in one whose gestation lasted two and a half years and who was born more than two and a half years after his father's death!
The number of those killed by him, apart from wars, has been written as one hundred and twenty thousand. When he perished, his prison held fifty thousand men and thirty thousand women, of whom 16,000 were naked and bare, and the custom of that accursed man was to imprison women, men and children together; his prison had no roof.
He martyred a great many of the friends and Shi'a of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), among them Kumayl ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i, Qanbar, the servant of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari, whom he whipped so much to make him curse Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) while he kept reciting the Imam's virtues, until Hajjaj ordered that he be martyred. He cut off the hands and feet of Yahya ibn Umm Tawil, one of the disciples of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), until he was martyred. He also martyred Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and 15 days after his killing, Hajjaj reached his end. Hajjaj was afflicted with the disease of akila, and a physician tied a piece of meat to a thread so that the accursed man would swallow it. The physician held the end of the thread, and after a moment pulled the thread and saw that little remained. His grave was concealed in Wasit and water was run over it, but in the time of al-Saffah his grave was found, and what remained was burned and scattered to the wind. He ruled in Iraq for twenty years, and his ill-fated life was 53 years.
sources: Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 471.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Mukhtar
events.text:
In the year 67 AH on such a day, Mukhtar ibn Abi Ubayd al-Thaqafi was martyred, and his tomb is beside the shrine of Muslim (AS) at the end of the Mosque of Kufa.
After martyring Mukhtar, Mus'ab ordered that his wife be arrested. She was a believing woman named Amra, daughter of Nu'man ibn Bashir al-Ansari. Mus'ab said: Disavow your husband. She said: How can I disavow one who fasted by day and stood in prayer by night, who shed his blood for God and the Prophet (SAWW), and who avenged the blood of the son of the Prophet (SAWW)? Mus'ab, with his sword drawn from its sheath, said: Then I will join you to your husband. Mukhtar's wife replied: After this, death is Paradise, and by God, I prefer nothing over my love for Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS).
In the heat of the day, in a plain between Hira and Kufa, her hands and feet were bound, then her neck was struck and her head was severed from her body. This believing woman was the first woman martyr to be killed under torture for love of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 91-92. al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 157. Fayz al-'Allam: p. 33. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 386. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 215.
al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi: p. 40.

events.title: The Birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS)
events.text:
On the night of the middle of Ramadan in the third year AH, the second Imam of the Shi'a, Abu Muhammad Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), was born in the city of Medina.
His titles: Sayyid, Sibt, Amin, Hujja, Barr, Taqi, Zaki, Mujtaba, Zahid.
His blessed complexion was red and white, his blessed eyes were wide and black. His blessed cheeks were smooth, his beard thick and the hair of his head curly. His blessed neck shone with light and purity like polished silver; he was of medium height with broad shoulders and was the most handsome-faced of all people. He used to dye his hair often, and his noble body was of utmost delicacy. On the seventh day after his birth, his mother Fatima al-Zahra (AS) wrapped that blessed newborn in a piece of silk cloth that Gabriel (AS) had brought for the Prophet (SAWW) from Paradise, and brought him to the noble Messenger of Islam (SAWW); the Prophet named him Hasan and sacrificed a sheep as his 'aqiqa.
sources: al-Irshad: vol. 2, p. 5. Fayz al-'Allam: p. 34. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 43, p. 250; vol. 95, p. 192. I'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 402. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 514. events.title: Muslim's (AS) Departure Toward Kufa
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, Aba Abd Allah (AS) (Imam Husayn) sent Muslim ibn Aqil (AS) to Kufa. He carried with him the replies to the letters of the Kufans, the substance of which was as follows: “I have sent to you my brother and cousin, the trusted one of my family, Muslim ibn Aqil. If he writes to me that the opinion of your wise men and notables has united on what you have written in your letters, I will come to you soon, God willing.”
sources: Fayz al-'Allam: p. 35.

events.title: The Arrival of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr in Egypt
events.text: On this day in the year 37 or 38 AH, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr entered Egypt as governor on behalf of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
sources: al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 190. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 213.

events.title: The Ascension (Mi'raj) of the Prophet
events.text:
The Ascension of the Prophet (SAWW) took place on such a day five years after the Prophetic mission (bi'tha), and the verse “Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque...” was revealed concerning it. The Ascension of the Prophet (SAWW) has also been reported on 21 Ramadan.
The Ascension is among the necessities of Islam, and it is established by the noble verses and mutawatir (widely transmitted) hadiths that God Almighty took the Messenger (SAWW) in a single night from sacred Mecca to the Farthest Mosque and from there to the heavens, to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary and the Supreme Throne; showed him the wonders of the creation of the heavens, imparted to him hidden secrets and infinite knowledge; and that he stood in worship of God Almighty in the Frequented House (Bayt al-Ma'mur) beneath the Throne, met the prophets (AS), entered Paradise, and beheld the abodes of the people of Paradise and the condition of those being punished.
Mutawatir hadiths indicate that his ascension was bodily, not spiritual, and in wakefulness, not in a dream. Other views on the determination of the day of the Ascension are as follows: 17 Ramadan, 12 years before the Hijra; 17 Rabi' al-Awwal before the Hijra; 17 Rajab before the Hijra; 17 Ramadan, 5 years before the Prophetic mission; 27 Ramadan; 21 Ramadan.
There are also several views regarding the place from which the Prophet (SAWW) began his journey to the Ascension: from the house of Khadija (AS), from the house of Umm Hani, the sister of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), from the Valley (Shi'b) of Abu Talib (AS).
Imam Sadiq (AS) said: The Almighty took the Messenger (SAWW) to heaven one hundred and twenty-four times, and each time He emphasized and counseled him concerning the guardianship (wilayah) and Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and the other pure Imams (AS) more than the other obligations.

events.title: The Battle of Badr
events.text:
On a Friday in the second year of the Hijra, the Great Battle of Badr took place. The 18th or 19th of this month has also been mentioned. The number of Muslims was 313 and the number of their martyrs 9 to 14, and the number of unbelievers was 950. The unbelievers killed numbered 70, and the Muslims also took 70 prisoners. Of the 70 unbelievers killed, 35 were slain by Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
In this battle Abu Jahl was also killed. Abu Jahl, Hisham ibn Mughira al-Makhzumi, was one of the fiercest enemies of the Prophet (SAWW). Although his name was Hisham, because of his extreme wickedness and ugly character he was given the epithet Abu Jahl (“Father of Ignorance”). Abu Jahl was the one who greatly harassed and tormented the Messenger of God (SAWW) in Mecca. He threw a camel's afterbirth on the Prophet's blessed head. He threw ashes and dust on the Prophet's blessed head. He struck a stone against his blessed tooth, and accused him of lying and madness. He martyred Sumayya, the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, after much torture, with a spear that he thrust into her thigh.
In the Battle of Badr, two Ansari brothers (Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh), because of what they had heard about his harassment of the Prophet (SAWW), decided to kill him. In any case they struck him several blows, and the hand of one of the two brothers was cut off and hung by the skin, but when he saw that his hand was hindering the fight against Abu Jahl and his supporters, he placed it under his foot and suddenly tore it off his body, and then they struck Abu Jahl to the ground.
After the battle, the Prophet (SAWW) said: Let someone bring news of Abu Jahl. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud went and placed his foot on his chest. Abu Jahl regained consciousness and said: You have stepped on a high place; I wish my killer were not a farmer (alluding to the Ansar). Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud severed his head from his body, brought it to the Prophet (SAWW) and threw it before his feet. The Prophet (SAWW) offered thanks to God, and God sent down His help upon the Prophet (SAWW), and he said: Today is a day of festival, and one must give thanks to God for the blessing He has bestowed on the people of faith.

events.title: The Killing of Aisha
events.text:
On the night of 17 Ramadan in the year 58 AH in Medina, Aisha, daughter of Abu Bakr, was killed at the hands of Muawiya and received the reward of her deeds. Two other views on this are 29 Rajab and the end of Dhu al-Hijja.
The Prophet (SAWW) wished that while he was alive he would see the death and burial of Aisha. Ibn Abi al-Hadid says: If the second caliph had been in the place of Ali (AS), he would have cut Aisha to pieces. When Muawiya wanted to take the pledge of allegiance from the people for his son Yazid, Aisha rejected it and threatened Muawiya, saying: You killed my brother Muhammad, and now you take allegiance for Yazid? Muawiya feared that she might stir up sedition. So he dug a pit in his house and filled it with quicklime, spread a precious carpet over it, and invited Aisha to his house at the time of the night prayer. When Aisha entered, Muawiya offered her a seat on that platform. As soon as she sat on it, it gave way and she fell into the pit and perished. Muawiya had set several poisoned spears in the pit, and when Aisha fell in, she was finished at once.
During the life of the Prophet (SAWW), Aisha behaved improperly toward him. She treated Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), Lady Siddiqa (AS) and the wives of the Prophet (SAWW) with ugly and spiteful conduct. The event of the Camel and the killing of about twenty thousand Muslims because of her sedition are among her well-known deeds.
When Lady Zahra (AS) was martyred, the wives of the Messenger of God (SAWW) came to offer condolences to Amir al-Mu'minin, except Aisha, who feigned illness and said something indicating her joy.
One of the clearest signs of her hatred and spite toward Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) was that she named her servant “Abd al-Rahman” and said: I gave this name out of my love for the killer of Ali ibn Abi Talib, namely Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam.

events.title: The Striking of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
events.text:
On 19 Ramadan in the year 40 AH, during the dawn prayer in the Mosque of Kufa, a blow was struck on the blessed head of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) with a poisoned sword by the impure hand of the hypocrite Ibn Muljam.
On 13 Ramadan in the year 40 AH, His Eminence Mawla al-Muwahhidin Ali ibn Abi Talib, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), after finishing the Battle of Nahrawan, foretold his own martyrdom. On that day, from the pulpit, after speaking about the truths of Islam, at the end of his blessed remarks he said to his son Imam Hasan Mujtaba (AS): How many days of the blessed month of Ramadan have passed until today? Imam Mujtaba (AS) said: Thirteen days have passed. He asked Imam Husayn (AS): How many days remain? Imam Husayn (AS) said: Seventeen days remain. At this, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) took hold of his blessed beard and said: It is near that this hair of mine will be dyed with the blood of my head.
On the night of 16 Ramadan in the year 40 AH, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) saw the Prophet (SAWW) in a dream, and the Prophet gave him glad tidings of the nearness of their meeting in Paradise; Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) informed his daughter Umm Kulthum (AS). On the nineteenth night, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) broke his fast at the house of Umm Kulthum (AS).
On the night of 19 Ramadan in the year 40 AH, Wardan and Shabib, who had accompanied Ibn Muljam in the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), were killed in the course of the struggle.
In the year 40, a group of the Khawarij gathered in Mecca and wept over those slain at Nahrawan. Three of them made a pact to kill Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), Amr ibn al-As and Muawiya in a single night.
Ibn Muljam took on the killing of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), entered Kufa, and with the help of Qatam bint al-Akhdar, whom Ibn Muljam intended to marry, and with the collaboration of Shabib ibn Bujra and Wardan ibn Mujalid, carried out his plan. On the morning of the nineteenth, after the dawn call to prayer, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) entered the mosque, and his dear voice rose with “O people, prayer!”
Then he began the prayer. When, in the first rak'a, he raised his head from prostration, Shabib attacked him, but his sword missed. Immediately Ibn Muljam, God's curse upon him, attacked, and his sword split the blessed head of the Imam, and his noble beard was dyed with the blood of his blessed head, and his blessed voice rose: “In the name of God, by God, and upon the creed of the Messenger of God — by the Lord of the Ka'ba, I have succeeded.”
The voice of Gabriel rose: “By God, the pillars of guidance have been demolished, the banners of piety have been effaced, and the firm handle has been broken; the cousin of the Chosen One has been killed, the chosen successor has been killed, Ali the Approved has been killed, the most wretched of the wretched has killed him.”
sources: al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 139. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 213.

events.title: The Conquest of Mecca
events.text:
The Conquest of Mecca took place in the year 8 AH. In this great conquest the number of Muslims was 12,000, and the martyrs were 2. The reason for the martyrdom of those two was that they were not with the army and had entered from the far end of Mecca, and were therefore attacked and martyred.
On this day, by the blessed command of the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) placed his blessed foot on the noble shoulder of the most honored of creation in order to break the idols that were in the Ka'ba.
Majlisi (RA), quoting from Tarikh al-Tabari, relates: When the Prophet (SAWW) decided to march toward Mecca, he summoned Umar and said to him: Go to Mecca and inform the nobles of Quraysh of our situation. Umar said: I fear for my life from the nobles of Quraysh!
When the Muslims entered Mecca they chanted: “al-Yawm yawm al-malhama” — “Today is the day of slaughter.” The Prophet (SAWW) said: Change the slogan and say: “al-Yawm yawm al-marhama” — “Today is the day of mercy.” Then he said: Abu Sufyan and his house are safe, and whoever enters his house is safe. He also said: Everyone is safe except one man named “Habbar ibn al-Aswad,” and some have also mentioned Muawiya. The Prophet said: “Even if Habbar is clinging to the curtain of the Ka'ba, kill him”?!
The reason for this severe treatment of Habbar was that in one of the Muslims' battles against the unbelievers of Quraysh, a number of the unbelievers were taken prisoner, and among the prisoners was the great son-in-law of the Prophet (SAWW), the husband of his daughter Zaynab. The Prophet said: Whoever sends a ransom, we will free his prisoner. Among what was sent from Mecca as ransom was the necklace of Lady Khadija (AS), which she had given to her daughter Zaynab. When the Prophet (SAWW) saw that necklace, he remembered Lady Khadija (AS) and wept. Then he asked the Muslims to give up that ransom, the keepsake of Khadija (AS), to him, and they agreed. Then it was agreed that the prisoners would be freed, in return for which any Muslim woman in Mecca who had accepted Islam would be free to come if she wished.
It was arranged that Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) would go and bring the litter (howdah) of the Fatimas. He went alone and brought Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet (SAWW), and the other Hashimite women. When they had gone a little way out of Mecca, Abu Sufyan, God's curse upon him, said: Her cousin Muhammad (SAWW) led your young men astray and they became Muslims. Now this young man, that is Ali (AS), has come in broad daylight and is taking away his relatives. Block his way.
They came to prevent him. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) defended himself. Some were wounded and some reached their end; meanwhile Habbar ibn al-Aswad attacked the litter of the Hashimite women and thrust a spear at the litter of Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet (SAWW).
Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) attacked Habbar and put him to flight. Zaynab was frightened in this attack, and since she was six months pregnant, when they entered Medina, after some time she miscarried and Zaynab passed from the world. The Prophet (SAWW) said: “The blood of Habbar ibn al-Aswad is licit to shed,” and that whoever sees him anywhere should kill him. Ibn Abi al-Hadid says to his teacher: The Prophet (SAWW) deemed the shedding of Habbar's blood permissible because of terrifying Zaynab and causing her miscarriage. If the Prophet (SAWW) were alive, would he not deem permissible the shedding of the blood of the one who terrified Fatima (AS)?

events.title: The Martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
events.text:
The Imam of the God-fearing, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), was martyred on the night of the twenty-first of Ramadan, around the break of dawn, at the age of 63 years. On the twentieth of Ramadan the effects of the poison appeared in the blessed feet of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and his blessed feet swelled. On the twenty-first night the effect of the poison on the blessed body of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) increased greatly. The Imam gathered his children and family, bade them farewell, and gave his bequests. That night, whatever food and drink they brought, he did not take; his blessed lips moved in remembrance of God, and sweat like pearls poured from his noble forehead, which he wiped away with his blessed hand.
He said to Imam Mujtaba (AS): I entrust you to your brother Husayn (AS). To the other children, who were not from Fatima Zahra (AS), he said: I entrust you to obedience to Hasan and Husayn. Then he said: “May God grant you good patience. Tonight I depart from among you and join my beloved Muhammad Mustafa (SAWW), as he promised me.” The sound of weeping rose from the Ahl al-Bayt. Then he gave instructions to Imam Mujtaba (AS) concerning the washing, shrouding, prayer and place of burial, and spoke some words about Karbala with Imam Husayn (AS) and Lady Zaynab (AS).
After bidding farewell to everyone, he stretched his blessed hands and feet toward the qibla and said: “I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger,” and they closed his blessed eyes, and he blessed Paradise with his arrival.
The sound of lamentation and weeping rose from the house of the Imam. When the people of Kufa learned of it, the sound of wailing and cries rose from the whole city, like the day the Prophet (SAWW) passed away. That night the horizons of the sky changed, the earth trembled, and the sound of the glorification and sanctification of the angels was heard from the air.
Then they began to wash his body. After the washing and shrouding, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (AS) lifted the back of the bier as the Imam had instructed, and the front of the bier moved by itself, until it came down at a place. After the prayer over him was performed by Imam Mujtaba (AS), they dug a little beneath the bier and found a grave already prepared, inside which was a copper or clay tablet on which was written: “In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. This is a grave that the Prophet Noah dug for the righteous servant of God, Ali ibn Abi Talib.” They buried his pure body, and in accordance with his bequest they concealed his blessed grave, until in the time of Harun it became known to all. The children of the Imam from various wives number 28 daughters and sons. Five of them are the children of Lady Siddiqa Tahira Fatima Zahra (AS): Imam Hasan, Imam Husayn, Zaynab al-Kubra, Umm Kulthum and Muhsin (AS), who, during pregnancy, at six months, was martyred by the hypocrites in the incident of the attack on the house of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). Abbas (AS), Ja'far, Uthman and Abd Allah were martyred at Karbala; their mother was Umm al-Banin. The rest of the Imam's children are from other wives.
When the news of the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) reached Aisha, she became so happy that she involuntarily recited a verse of poetry, and then said: Who killed Ali? They answered: Ibn Muljam. She said: May his mouth not be filled with dust (an expression implying that he did well).
On the night of 21 Ramadan, Jesus son of Mary (AS) was raised to heaven; and on the same night Moses son of Imran and Joshua son of Nun (AS) passed away.

events.title: The Pledge of Allegiance to Imam Mujtaba (AS)
events.text: On this day, after the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), the people pledged allegiance to Imam Hasan (AS).
sources: Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 538.

events.title: The Killing of Ibn Muljam
events.text: On this day Ibn Muljam was sent to Hell with a single stroke of the sword. After Ibn Muljam was killed, the people rushed upon the accursed, immoral Qatam, sent her to her end with the sword, and burned her body outside Kufa. Ibn Battuta, who died in the year 779 AH, said: When I traveled to Kufa, to the west of the Jabbana of Kufa, in a white land I saw a very black patch of ground and asked the reason. They said: This is the grave of Ibn Muljam. It is the custom of the people of Kufa that every year they bring a great deal of firewood and burn it at this spot for 7 days.
sources: Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 410.
Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 409.

events.title: The Revelation of the Qur'an
events.text: This is the night of the revelation of the Qur'an, and according to one view it was on the night of 24 Ramadan.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 10. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 88, p. 7.

events.title: The Death of Abu Lahab
events.text: On this day, and according to one view on 25 Ramadan, Abu Lahab reached his end.
sources: Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 463.

events.title: The Innovation of the Tarawih Prayer by Umar
events.text: In this month in the year 14 AH, he introduced the innovation of performing the voluntary (nafila) prayer in congregation, then appointed one man as prayer leader for the men and another man for the women.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 31, p. 12, footnote.

events.title: The Rain Prayer by the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text: In the month of Ramadan in the sixth year AH, a severe drought occurred in Medina; the Prophet (SAWW) prayed for rain, and rain came.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 376.
